topic: Running a CAS stateless test directly via `tests/clickhouse-test` agains
canonical_claim: Running a CAS stateless test directly via `tests/clickhouse-test` against a manually-started `clickhouse-server` binary (no configured praktika lane) requires exporting `CLICKHOUSE_USER_FILES` to match the server's actual data path; the harness's default `/var/lib/clickhouse/user_files` mismatch makes the pool directory invisible to the server, producing `Unknown disk` with `baseline=0 after_insert=0`.

topic: TLA+ models run from `docs/superpowers/models/` with the TLC jar expecte
canonical_claim: TLA+ models run from `docs/superpowers/models/` with the TLC jar expected at `../../../tmp/tla2tools.jar` (v2.19) and the Apalache binary at `../../../tmp/apalache/bin/apalache-mc` (v0.58.0+); runners are either suite runners that take no arguments and assert every expected outcome by invariant/property name (`run_refsnaplog.sh`, `run_mount.sh`, `run_buildrootprecommit.sh`, etc.) or single-config drivers that take a cfg as `$1` and assert nothing themselves (`run_tlc.sh`, `run_gc_partmanifest.sh`, `run_ackfloor.sh`).

topic: Attributing S3 PUTs to MergeParts/MutatePart requires a query_id-decodin
canonical_claim: Attributing S3 PUTs to MergeParts/MutatePart requires a query_id-decoding technique because part_log's own ProfileEvents never captures a nonzero PUT for those event types: the upload count is recovered by matching blob_storage_log's synthetic `<table_uuid>::<part_name>` query_id against part_log by part name (documented in the analyzing-cas-health skill and utils/ca-soak/scenarios/BACKLOG.md's 2026-07-19 'S3 PUT budget' entry).

topic: The soak harness's quiescence protocol before any checkpoint assertion i
canonical_claim: The soak harness's quiescence protocol before any checkpoint assertion is: pause all workers; `SYSTEM SYNC REPLICA` on both nodes and wait for `system.replication_queue` to be empty; wait for every `system.mutations` row to be `is_done` with no active `system.merges`; run `OPTIMIZE TABLE ... FINAL` plus `ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE TTL`; then drive CA GC to fixpoint by polling until the pool object set and `ca-fsck`'s `unreachable` field stop changing across successive rounds.

topic: The praktika stateless job name that works for local CAS validation is `
canonical_claim: The praktika stateless job name that works for local CAS validation is `"Stateless tests (arm_binary, parallel)"`.

topic: The CAS pool-member decommission SQL surface exposes `SYSTEM CONTENT ADD
canonical_claim: The CAS pool-member decommission SQL surface exposes `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED DROP POOL MEMBER`, backed by a disks facade command `ca-drop-member`; validated end-to-end on a 2-node RustFS integration test (kill -> lease expiry -> drop -> heal -> fsck-clean -> BAD_ARGUMENTS flow).

topic: The scenario harness's `observe
canonical_claim: The scenario harness's `observe.pool_shape()` probe had a `timeout N cd <dir> && find ...` bug: `timeout` cannot exec the `cd` shell-builtin, so `&&` short-circuited and the probe silently returned no `_total`; fixed to `timeout N sh -c '<cd && find | xargs stat>'`.

topic: CAS's `contentAddressedFsckColumns` SQL row (the `SYSTEM
canonical_claim: CAS's `contentAddressedFsckColumns` SQL row (the `SYSTEM ... FSCK` output) does not surface `lifeless_keys` even though the function's own comment states every term of `FsckReport::clean` must appear there; the comment claiming the summary is derived mechanically from `clean()`'s field set was false — the actual implementation is five hand-listed field names, so the enforcement mechanism the comment describes does not exist.

topic: A reviewer sub-agent must deliver findings BOTH as a durable file AND in
canonical_claim: A reviewer sub-agent must deliver findings BOTH as a durable file AND in its final message; message-only delivery risks the findings existing nowhere durable and never reaching the implementer, while file-only delivery has separately caused lost verdicts.

topic: The `utils/ca-soak/scenarios` adversarial card suite (S01-S35) stresses
canonical_claim: The `utils/ca-soak/scenarios` adversarial card suite (S01-S35) stresses one hard condition per scenario; many gtest regression pins originated as soak findings, e.g. S04/S04b became `gc_undercount_repro.cpp` and the TRUNCATE op-450 stall became `truncate_reclaim.cpp`.

topic: S42 fault-injection coverage
canonical_claim: S42 arms `memory_tracker_fault_probability` through driver URL parameters and pairs it with `max_untracked_memory=0` so small allocations reach the memory tracker. S42 is intended to fault allocations through the per-query `memory_tracker_fault_probability` setting and thread creation through `cannot_allocate_thread_fault_injection_probability`, then verify that durable CAS state, replicas, fsck, and post-restart views remain consistent even when queries fail.

topic: fsck timeout scalability
canonical_claim: The D1 report identifies fsck scalability as follow-up work: `clickhouse-disks fsck` timed out after more than 180 seconds on a pool with approximately 1.7 million rows, although the final converge fsck completed cleanly. The flat 180-second fsck budget can time out once the ref space is large enough that the check for stuck blobs stops running at the scale where it is needed.

topic: `CasRefCodec
canonical_claim: `CasRefCodec.EncodeAllowsExactlyMaxRemovalBytes` could not be classified from the archived log because it ended after the `[ RUN      ]` line without an exception, sanitizer report, result, or exit code; it requires an isolated ASan run with preserved exit status, stderr, and host OOM or signal evidence.

topic: The relink unhappy-path test must drive a pending target-name mutation,
canonical_claim: The relink unhappy-path test must drive a pending target-name mutation, a wedge, and a lost fence, then assert severity, transient-state messaging, no same-source byte re-request, and convergence of the retry cycle.

topic: The required Stage B tests include old-file hiding across drop and rebir
canonical_claim: The required Stage B tests include old-file hiding across drop and rebirth, stale readers and delayed writers after rebirth, resumed stale cleanup, zero catalog requests on hot paths, unchanged rewrite/append/remove/dedup-rotation request counts, LIST-independent recovery, missing and conflicting `_ckpt.life_epoch`, rejection of legacy keys, and compile-time absence of namespace-only key overloads.

topic: The T14 audit leaves the identity of the `pthread_mutex_lock` term open
canonical_claim: The T14 audit leaves the identity of the `pthread_mutex_lock` term open because only the top frame was captured; the addendum must retain full symbolized stacks and filter `trace_type='Real'` with top frame `pthread_mutex_lock`.

topic: The T14 audit leaves the `mkdir` to `std::filesystem::create_directories
canonical_claim: The T14 audit leaves the `mkdir` to `std::filesystem::create_directories` attribution open; a deeper or focused background profile must determine whether the directory-creation signal survives bounded rounds and which layer creates the directories.

topic: The frontier-attribution spike must classify every unproven namespace as
canonical_claim: The frontier-attribution spike must classify every unproven namespace as post-LIST append above frozen tail, probe-budget exhaustion, effective hold, genuine gap, undecodable `_ckpt`, or whole-fold abort before destruction is enabled.

topic: The LIST-as-journal detector had fired 14 times but still needed lease i
canonical_claim: The LIST-as-journal detector had fired 14 times but still needed lease identity recorded at both ends of the enumeration to distinguish an actual listing hole from concurrent deletion.

topic: The 600-second product fsck deadline was insufficient for a roughly 29 G
canonical_claim: The 600-second product fsck deadline was insufficient for a roughly 29 GiB pool: a measured run took 731.1 seconds and returned `TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED` without a `reachable=` line.

topic: S22 requires a fault-injecting proxy between the CA disk endpoint and Ru
canonical_claim: S22 requires a fault-injecting proxy between the CA disk endpoint and RustFS to inject `503 SlowDown`, `429 Too Many Requests`, latency, and mid-response TCP resets; toxiproxy covers TCP faults but not HTTP status injection.

topic: S27 requires an instrumented S3 proxy that can duplicate root-shard LIST
canonical_claim: S27 requires an instrumented S3 proxy that can duplicate root-shard LIST keys, omit a continuation token, or change an otherwise stable list token so `listRootShardTokens` conservative rereads can be exercised.

topic: GC verification must retain a strict grouped enumeration of all key clas
canonical_claim: GC verification must retain a strict grouped enumeration of all key classes and add negative controls for ambiguous-send reuse, hidden checkpoints, rebirth cleanup omissions, asymmetric REBUILD omissions, and current-epoch manifest growth.

topic: The verification model must include one shared blob and pool-wide in-deg
canonical_claim: The verification model must include one shared blob and pool-wide in-degree and retirement state, with controls for late +1, catalog transitions, forced REBUILD after a hold, classification-4 codec limits, stale reads, duplicate nomination, token ABA, and _ckpt-absent decommission finalization.

topic: Verification must force missing prior seals, disappearing held witnesses
canonical_claim: Verification must force missing prior seals, disappearing held witnesses, an incarnation-dropping key builder, and an old-generation wedge result after successor seal adoption; recovery and wedge installs need a generation recheck under the install lock.

topic: Audit every public operation in ContentAddressedMetadataStorage, Content
canonical_claim: Audit every public operation in ContentAddressedMetadataStorage, ContentAddressedTransaction, and object-storage entry points by latency class, S3 round trips, state dependence, and lock context.

topic: Audit every mutex, SharedMutex, and condition variable in the CA tree fo
canonical_claim: Audit every mutex, SharedMutex, and condition variable in the CA tree for protected state, longest critical-section operation, waiters, cutoff or indefinite-wedge behavior, and fencing interaction.

topic: `CasRefCatalogFormat
canonical_claim: `CasRefCatalogFormat.RemovalStartedRoundIsRequiredExactlyForRemoving` directly invokes a `LOGICAL_ERROR`-throwing site under `DEBUG_OR_SANITIZER_BUILD`, where the process aborts instead of throwing; the planned hygiene fix is to guard the throwing arm and add a `Cas*DeathTest` arm using `EXPECT_DEATH`.

topic: The recommended remediation order for the LOGICAL_ERROR ASan triage is:
canonical_claim: The recommended remediation order for the LOGICAL_ERROR ASan triage is: (1) swap the one Class A hook from `LOGICAL_ERROR` to `S3_ERROR`; (2) convert the 19 direct Class B negative assertions to `EXPECT_DEATH`, including the worker-thread heartbeat case; (3) repair the three incidental teardown fixtures so the primary test cleans up validly while the release guard gets an isolated death assertion; (4) remove the Class D test from the logical-error list pending a captured, reproducible failure.

canonical_claim: The recommended CA transient-classifier fix (routing `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp:1111`, `:1163`, and `CasMountRuntime.cpp:106` through a new `throwCasTransientUnavailable`) has carry-along updates: `utils/ca-soak/soak/cluster.py:215`; `gtest_cas_operation_gate.cpp:182-217` (must split its shared-code contract asserting both `TransientNotLive` and `IdentityLost` throw 668); `gtest_cas_fsck.cpp:669`; `gtest_cas_gc_stop_start.cpp:472`; and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-cas-disk-lease-loss-throw-and-stop-verbs-design.md:56`.
